title: DGFiP's 'Foncier innovant' deep-learning detection of undeclared swimming pools: 20,000+ pools taxed for 2022, about €10 million for communes
summary: DGFiP deep-learning pool detection: 20,000+ pools taxed for 2022 (~€10m for communes); 150,000 taxable pools found across metropolitan France excluding Paris and overseas departments
account: France's Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) runs 'Foncier innovant': a deep-learning algorithm extracts building and pool outlines from public IGN aerial images, an automated check compares them with land-tax files, and a tax agent verifies every anomaly before the owner is contacted. DGFiP's October 2021 note says Capgemini provided project-management and build assistance and Google the cloud infrastructure and services for developing the AI models. The 2022 experiment in nine departments led to more than 20,000 pools being taxed for 2022, close to €10 million of extra revenue for the communes concerned (DGFiP, 2 June 2023); the sources give no other date for this result, so the date observed is the publication date of that announcement. The Sénat's April 2024 report puts the cost at €24 million. After generalization in 2023, the first pass across metropolitan France, excluding Paris and the overseas departments (DROM), detected 150,000 untaxed taxable pools, which the Sénat report calls 'potentiellement taxables'; industrialization began in June 2024.
purpose: Detect undeclared pools and buildings from aerial imagery to bring them into the local property-tax base
system: Foncier innovant (DGFiP): open-source deep-learning segmentation of IGN orthophotos cross-checked with cadastral and tax files
developer: DGFiP (Délégation à la transformation numérique) with Capgemini (assistance à maîtrise d'ouvrage et maîtrise d'œuvre) and Google (cloud infrastructure and AI-model development services)
domain: Tax administration: local property tax base
taxonomy_note: Closest fit; the benefit is additional lawful tax revenue for communes and fairer tax bases, which the taxonomy does not name.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: aggregate program results; no discrete attributable event.

ai_role.statement: Official sources describe the pipeline (AI detection, automated file check, systematic human verification, owner contact) and attribute the taxed pools to it, but no evaluation isolates the algorithm's contribution from the human verification and declaration campaign. The AN written answer of 14 Dec 2021 confirms DGFiP's use of AI on IGN imagery and that contractors do not access tax data.
